title: Tech Note: 4DAF Optimizer – Part 1
author: Tom Fitch, Technical Support Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note introduces the 4DAF Optimizer, a companion utility that lets developers strip unused 4D Ajax Framework JavaScript files from the 'js' folder and rebuild a slimmer 'framework.js' bundle, improving page load times for custom 4DAF-based pages by selecting only the objects/features actually used (Calendar, Data Grid, Data Tree, DDW, Data/Image Matrix, plus sidebar/taskbar/hierarchical list features). It is entirely specific to the discontinued 4DAF/4D Web 2.0 Pack's asset-loading architecture, so the tool and workflow have no modern equivalent. The general concept — bundling/tree-shaking only the JS actually needed by a page to reduce load time — is exactly the problem solved today by modern JS bundlers (webpack, esbuild, Vite, Rollup), making this note an interesting historical precursor to now-standard tooling.
related_updates: 4D Ajax Framework and 4D Web 2.0 Pack were discontinued and are no longer part of any current 4D product
The manual JS-selection/bundling problem this tool solved is now addressed by modern JavaScript bundlers with automatic tree-shaking (e.g. webpack, Rollup, esbuild, Vite)
